input: Back up all phone contacts to the cloud

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: iPhone and Android have completely different native backup paths (iCloud vs Google Contacts), so the phone type determines the whole approach.
Knowing whether this is a one-time backup or an ongoing automatic sync changes whether we set up a recurring process or just do it once.
If the contacts belong to a personal account vs a work account (e.g., Exchange, Microsoft 365), the tools and permissions involved differ significantly.
The preferred cloud destination (Google, iCloud, Outlook, a third-party app) determines which specific steps to follow.
The user may already have a cloud account set up, or may need to create one — this determines how many prerequisite steps are needed.
Understanding what 'done well' means — e.g., contacts accessible on another device, exportable as a file, or shareable — shapes how to verify the backup worked.
Some users want full automation with no manual steps; others prefer to export a file they control. This affects which solution to recommend.

gold.taskTitle: Back up all phone contacts to the cloud
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to save their phone's contacts to a cloud service so they are preserved and accessible beyond the device.

questions.title: What type of phone do you have, iPhone or Android?
questions.description: Identifies the operating system, which determines the entire backup workflow and available native tools.

questions.title: Should this be a one-time backup or automatic ongoing sync?
questions.description: Determines whether to configure a recurring sync process or just perform a single manual export.

questions.title: Are these personal contacts, work contacts, or both?
questions.description: Clarifies account ownership, which affects which service handles the backup and what permissions or policies apply.

questions.title: Which cloud service do you want to back up to?
questions.description: Identifies the target destination (e.g., Google Contacts, iCloud, Outlook, a third-party app) to tailor the step-by-step instructions.

questions.title: Do you already have a cloud account set up and ready?
questions.description: Establishes whether account creation and login steps need to be included before the backup itself can begin.

questions.title: How will you confirm the backup actually worked correctly?
questions.description: Defines the success condition — e.g., viewing contacts on another device, receiving a confirmation email, or downloading an export file.

questions.title: Do you prefer full automation or keeping a manual file you control?
questions.description: Captures the user's preference between a hands-off sync solution versus an exportable file (e.g., .vcf) they store themselves.
